THE RULE THAT GOVERNS THIS BOOK: A SURNAME IS ALMOST NEVER ONE MAN, SO KEY BY DEFAULT AND ALIAS ONLY ON PROOF. There is no 'Bloom' default and 4:38 -- SLIEVE BLOOM, the mountains in Offaly -- is deliberately not keyed. THE SURNAME DEDALUS HAS NOW CHANGED HANDS TWICE: episodes 1-2 key it to STEPHEN, episodes 6-8 to his father SIMON, and EPISODE 9 IS THE SON AGAIN (9:136, 9:181, 9:224, 9:355 -- Mr Dedalus, your views are most illuminating). EPISODE 10 WILL GIVE IT A THIRD OWNER: the Dedalus daughters. A test pins every exception.

EPISODE 9 IS THE HARDEST SO FAR AND ITS PATTERNS WILL RECUR. HAMLET IS THE PRINCE, THE DEAD KING AND THE PLAY IN THE SAME PARAGRAPH, keyed by occurrence, with None for the play. RICHARD is the king, the brother and MR BEST'S OWN NAME in one speech (9:342). EDMUND is the bastard in King Lear and the brother dying in Southwark in one paragraph (9:345). WILL is the auxiliary verb five times and the man four times. BEST is the adjective in fourteen paragraphs elsewhere in the book (best value in Dub) so only three are keyed. LUCY was aliased, caught S. LUCY at 12:513, and is keyed now -- RUN THE OCCURRENCE LIST ON EVERY ALIAS, NOT JUST EVERY KEY.

A GUARD TRAP WORTH REMEMBERING: the alias guard is (?<![A-Za-z])...(?![A-Za-z]) for keyed tables but (?<!\w)...(?!\w) for aliases, and AN APOSTROPHE AND A HYPHEN ARE NOT WORD CHARACTERS, so an alias 'Flynn' binds every O'FLYNN and an alias 'Bacon' would bind Rutland-Bacon-Southampton-Shakespeare. Bare FLYNN is keyed paragraph by paragraph in episode 8 for that reason.

THE MODERN EDITION IS A REWRITE AND CHANGES THE CAST OF A PARAGRAPH IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. It DELETES names (Chrysostomos 1:9, Mercury 1:293, Loyola 1:101, Adam Findlater and Dan Tallon 4:37, Hanlon 4:13, Wren 6:204, the Joe Miller 7:293, mother Dana 9:157, Aubrey 9:294) and SUPPLIES names Joyce did not write (Aristotle 3:0, Brian Boru 3:57, Deasy 3:10, Queen Victoria 3:94, M'Coy 5:27, Daniel O'Connell 6:106/6:277/6:278, Madame Bloom 6:104, Shakespeare 6:333, Martha 6:386, Nannetti 7:42/7:62, Bloom 7:67, Patrick Dignam 7:99, Gallaher 7:358, Mario 7:27, Long John Fanning 7:45, Boylan 8:35/8:255, Lot's wife 8:35, Charles Stewart Parnell 8:141, Reuben J. IT ALSO SPLITS JOYCE'S COMPOUNDS, WHICH MAKES A NAME BINDABLE THAT WAS NOT: 'Jesusmario' (7:27) becomes 'Jesus-Mario', 'pseudomalachi' (9:194) 'false Malachi', 'Sonmulligan' (9:331) 'Son-Mulligan', 'Rutlandbaconsouthamptonshakespeare' (9:328) 'Rutland-Bacon-Southampton-Shakespeare' and 'Besteglinton' (9:286) 'Best-Eglinton'. Five entities are reachable in one edition only: BRIAN BORU and LOT'S WIFE in the modern alone, ADAM FINDLATER, MOTHER DANA and JOHN AUBREY in the older alone.

A SILENT BINDER LIMITATION THAT APPLIES TO EVERY BOOK IN THIS LIBRARY: reviewed_aliases.py guards alias matches with \w, AND AN UNDERSCORE SATISFIES \w, so an alias whose occurrence sits inside Gutenberg italics (_like this_) BINDS NOTHING AND NOTHING REPORTS IT. Four cases, all keyed now: '_Los Demiurgos_' 3:1, '_Matcham's Masterstroke_' 4:162, '_That's not Mulcahy_' 6:325, '_Mr MacTrigger_' 8:208 and 8:223. The MacTrigger case was found by the omittedEntities line in the validation report and by nothing else -- READ THAT LINE ON EVERY BUILD. Over all 18 episodes the italic check also reports STEPHEN at 15:1133 (a stage direction, will need a key when Circe is read), PATRICE at 16:212 (which is NOT Patrice Egan but 'the faubourg Saint Patrice' and will need suppressing), and two play titles at 9:167 and 9:333 which are correct as they stand.

A SECOND SILENT FAILURE, FOUND IN EPISODE 8 AND NOW GUARDED: A REPEATED DICT LITERAL IN SPLIT OR PHRASE SHADOWS THE EARLIER ONE AND EVERY KEY IN IT CEASES TO EXIST. A duplicate 'Jack' table had been dropping the episode 7 keys for J. J. O'Molloy and a duplicate 'Paddy Dignam' table the episode 6 keys, with every test green. Tables.test_no_split_or_phrase_key_is_declared_twice now parses the source and fails on any repeated key. NEVER RE-DECLARE A TABLE -- MERGE INTO THE EXISTING LITERAL.
